items.title: Lawrence Duhé Interview, 1957-06-09
items.q: They had a colored man, Manuel Perez, all that was up there for them.

ctx.x: Yeah, the contract here says the New Orleans Jazz Band.

That must have been number two, but they had two orchestras left, but the Dixalan, you remember, bro, used to put that livery stable blue? Yeah, the rocker. Yeah, the rocker and shield. Yeah. Yeah, the ritual. They're still written in there. They had a colored man, Manuel Perez, all that was up there for them. These men, is it Mitchell Lacalze, C-A-L-Z-I?

That's the booker. He was the booker, and this Lee Krauss. Krauss, that's two partners. Two partners. They're the ones that booked you. That's correct. Into the deluxe. That's right. Yeah, that's so nice. We saw Louis Capard, have you seen him lately?

items.title: Lawrence Duhé Interview, 1960
items.q: But then that there wasn't a station in Chicago, such as the Dixieland, Manuel Perez, the Creole Band

ctx.x: Mr. Deer, we'd like for you to tell us, for instance, when these white musicians picked up jazz from the Cullen Boys.

Well, they used to come to those places nightly, and they got them so good so they'd say, Well, Deer, you want to take a walk around the block? I said, Yes. Go ahead. I'll rest you up. I'll play clarinet. And so the rest of the instruments, the other boys would rest them up like that. That's the way they started. Mr. Deer, when you were in the Warriors, did you happen to meet Buddy Bolger? I'm sure he must have run into him. Oh, yes. And New Orleans knows about him. There's no question to ask, because he started…
